newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Jan 23.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Jan 23.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

After spending more than A$300 million on three Melbourne properties, including A$243 million on the landmark 333 Collins Street office tower, Hong Kong's Kwok family could be looking at other acquisitions in Australia. The Kwoks built their fortune a century ago in a Sydney grocery and now control Wing On, Hong Kong's best known department stores. Page 1.

The Federal Government's heavy spending on private consultants is expected to increase again this year after an investigation by The Australian Financial Review found that spending on government consultancies used in 1995-96 rose by six per cent from the revious year. Advertising firm AIS Media and investment bank BZW Australia topped the list for consultancy fees, earning nearly A$18 million and A$11 million respectively. Page 1.

A one-off A$450 million increase in the value of non-residential construction related to Olympic projects in New South Wales has lifted the Westpac-Melbourne Institute leading index of economic activity to its highest level since 1994. Rising 0.6 per cen in November, the index measures where the economy will be in two or three quarters. Page 3.

Axiom Funds Management has sent about 30 potential buyers a 70-page confidential information memorandum and buyers have until February 7 to indicate the price they would be prepared to pay for the funds manager which manages A$17 billion in superannuation savings of New South Wales public servants. Page 15.

Some senior pay-TV industry players are pushing a plan to split the nation into geographical pay-TV monopolies and eliminate head-to-head competition between the Telstra and Optus networks. While the idea of splitting the nation into cable-TV monopolies as raised by Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting and its Optus Vision partners in late 1994 and subsequently rejected by the then Labor Government, a senior Government source said yesterday that the Coalition would at least consider the proposal. Page 15.

The board of Mount Edon Gold Mines Ltd has advised shareholders to take no action after Camelot Resources and its Canadian partner Teck Corporation yesterday launched a surprise A$158 million takeover bid for the miner following their acquisition of 14.5 percent of Mount Edon in on-market purchases. Page 15.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Bankers Trust senior economist David Bassanese said the early reaction of world financial markets to comments by United States Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that indicated a rise in interest rates in the United States was not imminent made it clear investors were relieved Greenspan did not repeat his December 5 observation about "irrational exuberance" that sent global sharemarkets into a spin. Page 21.

Coles Myer Ltd's Solomon Lew looks to purchase further shares in the company after a substantial shareholder notice was lodged to the Australian Stock Exchange yesterday. The notice says interests associated with Lew now own 141,539,746 Coles shares, about 250,000 shares more than was disclosed in the retailer's 1996 annual report. Page 21.

United States-based Showscan Entertainment will move into the competitive Australian market with the launch of giant screen cinemas through its venture partner Reality Cinemas. As senior Showscan officials arrive in Australia today to meet with government and industry representatives, its first Australian motion simulation theatre will open at Sydney's Darling Harbour in March. Page 23.

GNB Technologies head Graham Spurling will be replaced by the company's vice-president of automotive operations Tom Minner. The move, announced by company owner Pacific Dunlop Ltd, will see Spurling remain on the board of PacDun and take on a new role overseeing the introduction of world best practice at PacDun's manufacturing plants around the world. Page 23.

In a short statement to the Australian Stock Exchange, Victorian agricultural and fertiliser group Pivot Ltd increased its bid for Tasmanian miller Gibson's Ltd from A$4.80 to A$6 a share. The move may head off action by the revived Corporations and Secuities Panel. Page 23.

In a move that will lift RTZ-CRA's coal production in the United States to over 56 million tonnes, the Anglo-Australian company has purchased the sixth largest coal mine in the United States for A$128 million. The deal, through RTZ-CRA's wholly owned subidiary Kennecott Energy & Coal, is expected to win approval with the United States Government and should be finalised within several months. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

As the Australian gold sector undergoes a major shake-up that may see billions of dollars of assets change hands throughout 1997, Mount Edon Gold Mines is the subject of a joint A$158 million bid from fellow West Australian gold miner Camelot Resources and Canadian mining giant Teck Corporation. Page 25.

As the deadline for institutions to declare their hand for the sale of the Federal Government's troubled investment bank AIDC expires on Tuesday, Macquarie Bank is among about 10 financial institutions, mostly from overseas, interested in buying the AIDC. Page 25.

Former businessman and now prisoner Alan Bond has, from the Karnet Prison Farm, instructed a Sydney lawyer to oppose moves by the Australian Federal Police to get a secret report from the liquidator of his family company Dallhold Investments. Bond is serving a three year sentence for his part in the fraudulent valuation of the painting La Promenade and will be sentenced next month on separate charges relating to the stripping of more than A$1 billion from Bell Resources. Page 27.

The process of Futuris Corporation taking control of rural company Elders is expected to be dragged out because of a legal hitch related to an agreement signed by Futuris and Elders shareholder Sir James Goldsmith's General Oriental Investments. General Oriental accepted Futuris' offer on behalf of its 7.5 per cent stake in Elders. Page 27.

Optus Communications and other telecommunications companies ready to enter the deregulated market are expected to use an upcoming Senate committee as a forum to argue for more stringent controls on Telstra. The Senate committee will look into areas such as competition framework, overhead pay TV cabling, electro-magnetic radiation from mobile phone towers and union control over domestic wiring. Page 27.

The shares of Defiance Holdings, the 38 per cent shareholder in listed entity Defiance Mills, are set to be placed to institutional shareholders as Defiance Holdings is to be wound up. While a special meeting to decide the future of Defiance Holdings did not gain 75 per cent support to wind up the holding company, it was the unanimous view of all present that the holding company would be wound up in the near future. Page 27.
THE AGE

After Canadian-backed Western Australian miner Camelot Resources announced last night that it would make an offer for Mount Edon Gold at A$2.15 a share, Mount Edon managing director Tony Brennan advised shareholders no to sell, saying the offer was "unsolicited and opportunistic". Page B1.

Futuris Corp was last night set to move to compulsory acquisition of Elders Australia, after Sir James Goldsmith's General Oriental Investments agreed to sell its 7.3 per cent stake to Futuris. The stake will give Futuris more than 91 per cent of Elders, meaning remaining shareholders will have to accept Futuris' bid or sell their stock before the offer closes on 29 January. Page B1.

Despite purchasing Drummond Co Inc's subsidiary Caballo Rojo Inc and the Fort Union mine in the US for A$128 million, RTZ-CRA says it has no plans to abandon its underperforming New South Wales collieries, hoping to improve the return on its New South Wals assets and to improve the cost competitiveness of Hunter Valley mines. Page B1.

According to the Westpac/Melbourne institute leading index of economic activity released yesterday, the Australian economy is still moving at a slow pace but is likely to grow more strongly by late this year. The index rose 0.6 per cent in November to 1455 points, with a sharp rise in non-residential construction approvals being the key factor to boost the index. Page B1.

MasterCard International's planned A$150 million takeover of the British-based smart card group Mondex International could be in jeopardy, following the failure of talks with Australia's big four banks in Hong Kong. The ANZ, Westpac, National Australia ad Commonwealth banks are all shareholders in Mondex and own the rights to the technology in Australia, but because of unfavourable conditions imposed by MasterCard the banks are attempting to block the deal. Page B1.

The Australian Securities Commission's Corporations and Securities Panel will convene for the first time in six years tomorrow to study the circumstances of Pivot Nutrition's A$6 a share bid for Tasmanian flour miller Gibson's. Pivot's offer values Gibson's at A$27.4 million and adds 25 per cent to the previous offer of A$4.80 a share. Page B2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
